kind_of_no: no RV camping (tent-only; RV campground not being restored)
why: floridastateparks.org park page and Experiences & Amenities page (read 2026-10-30 in a browser): 'The park currently offers hike-in, tent-only campsites' with no hookups, and 'Effective July 12, 2026: All primitive camping and the Golden Orb hiking trail ... are closed for construction'; the state's US eDirect booking system (reserve.floridastateparks.org park 43, place API read 2026-10-30) lists one facility only, 'Orb Trail', unit type 'Tent Only'. The former drive-in oceanfront RV campground, closed since Irma (2017) and hit again by Ian (2022), appears on no agency page or booking channel; the agency's only reopening language is an undated pre-Ian recovery page ('In time, guests will be able to camp along the azure waters of Long Key once again'), and Florida Rambler (updated 2026-07-09) says 'there are now no plans to rebuild this campground'. No agency statement that RV camping will reopen, so not a temporarily-closed add.
name: Long Key State Park
flags: The July 12, 2026 'closed for construction' notice names only the primitive (hike-in tent) camping and the Golden Orb trail; nothing on the agency site says the construction is a rebuild of the RV loop. A call to the ranger station (305-664-4815) could settle whether an RV campground is planned; if the agency announces one, this becomes an add (ownership state, reserve.floridastateparks.org/Web/#!park/43).

Esri imagery of the old oceanfront loop (sat.py at 24.8120,-80.8255, rendered, read 2026-10-30; capture date unknown) shows the shore road with a few pull-outs and no RVs, pads or construction footprint.
RV Life still lists it (state, $$, ~$34, not flagged closed) and Campendium calls it permanently closed: both are stale directory records, not evidence either way.
No Google Maps check run: the agency pages settle it.
